nodes.statement: A finite digital event model with distinct source-issue, port-arrival, capture, invalidation, snapshot commit and designated read events. M_D is a device command copy, P_E a device state token; neither is named a human neural input. Availability, payload and actual occurrence are distinct.

nodes.statement: Capture writes the present source token only through an open gate; closure leaves the buffer unchanged; invalidation clears it. A snapshot copies both cells in one excluded/atomic macrostep, remains immutable, and must commit before the selected reads.
nodes.scope: Sequential reference semantics, not a measured hardware guarantee.
nodes.quantifier: All stated premises apply jointly to each declared instance; actual application remains independently open.

nodes.statement: For C1's both-read conclusion, the selected operation eagerly reads each committed snapshot cell; a missing cell uses an explicitly tagged absence default. Short-circuit, gate-reflex and live-port bypass are distinct classes.

nodes.quantifier: All stated premises apply jointly to each declared instance; actual application remains independently open.

nodes.statement: For every execution of the declared capture/invalidation/immutable-commit model, each snapshot cell contains the token from its last accepted capture surviving invalidation as of that snapshot's commit boundary, or absence. With the designated eager consumer actually reading that snapshot, it reads both intended tokens exactly when those two cells contain those actual tokens. Gate closure by itself neither clears nor revokes a retained token.

Eligibility, reset, timing, performance, access and reports are not new basal-experience gates.
Retained actual-token consumption requires grounded history; a warm buffer is not familiar H by label.
Timing and route premises must hold jointly in the same actual episode.
A source-send or gate label does not prove the targeted internal carrier was reached.
Overwrites and restoration can hide interventions; ordinary buffering is prior-covered.
A new header, equal values or trial label do not certify the intended source occurrence.
Arrival and capture must be justified at the actual target port.
A claimed predictive role requires its actual time-indexed bridge.
C1 transports correctly grounded complete-instance relations, not chosen feeling labels.
A formula in an admitted process does not independently select a separately actual sub-process.
No report-to-H bridge, conceptual-self equivalence or human neural-consumer identification is supplied.
